recipes.name: Butter Bean Burgers
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup vegetable oil, or as needed

steps.text: In a medium bowl, mash butter beans. Mix in onion, jalapeño, crackers, egg, cheese, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Divide into 4 equal parts and shape into patties.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat; use more or less oil to reach 1/4 inch in depth. Fry patties until golden, about 5 minutes on each side.

raw_recipe.headline: Butter Bean Burgers
raw_recipe.description: These butter bean burger patties combine jalapeño peppers, Cheddar cheese, and saltines to make a delicious vegetarian main dish or sandwich.

review.reviewBody: Wow, this was amazing!!! I did change quite a bit of things though... I cannot have gluten, so I omitted the saltine crackers and used crushed GF cornflakes instead. Also, we didn't have any butter beans so I used an equivalent amount of cooked, mashed lentils instead. After trying it both ways (lentils vs. butter beans) everyone liked the lentils much better! I also added a little diced green pepper and that REALLY enhanced the flavor, and I omitted the jalapeno pepper (don't like spice). I make this recipe ALL THE TIME, and we never get tired of it!!!!!!!!!!!

This one is a keeper. I took some suggestions from other reviewers like using bread crumbs instead of crackers and coating them with breadcrumbs and letting them sit in the fridge for a few hours.

Because of some digestion issues I have I omitted the jalapeno pepper and browned the onions before adding them. Just for fun I added a few dashes of liquid smoke. I have to stay away from fried foods so I put them in an iron skillet coated with nonstick spray in a 400 gas oven for ten minutes on each side. They turned out wonderful, with a slightly crunchy coating on the outside while moist and tender on the inside.

Nice base recipe. I added some things to make it more to my taste. I used part of an onion, part green pepper, some cumin, cayenne, parsley, and old bay. I only had northern beans so I used those. I also added some powdered parm and made these in to smaller patties since I figured they wouldn’t be as mushy in the middle and wouldn’t break apart. Rolled them in some bread crumbs and cooked them in a mix of butter and olive oil. Worked out great. I got about ten patties out of the mix. They came out nice and crunchy. I ate mine on a bun with lettuce, tomato, and mayo and my mom ate hers plain. She’s picky like a kid and she really liked them. She said she didn’t think they’d be as good without the breadcrumbs on the outside since she liked the crispy texture. Thanks for the beginning of a nice recipe.

I adore this recipe - it's so easy and so flavorful. I've made it with a variety of beans, and it always comes out yummy. I like to add Italian parsley, and extra saltines, extra cheese, and maybe extra spices. The burgers fall apart while frying. I've also tried them baked and they retain their shape a bit better that way. Delicious with garlic mayo, on ciabatta bread, with a pickle slice.

These were really nice. Minor changes made after reading other reviews: Used a clove of fresh garlic, 1/4 cup Italian breadcrumbs. After shaping I patted more bread crumbs on patties and refrigerated for a few hours. No issues with patties falling apart. My son said it tasted like mashed potato (that wasn't a complaint). Very mild flavor which can be suited according to one's own taste. Will certainly be making these again. Perhaps will try baking them next time as I don't like to fry - that was the only reason I gave it 4 stars rather than 5. Thanks for sharing!

It turned out great but I had to make a few changes. I used 1/4 cup of plain bread crumbs , added 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp chili powder and used grated cheddar instead of shredded cheese so it would bind a little easier. I made the patties and put it in the fridge to set for 20 minutes or so before sauteing in an iron skillet. I had some cooked fresh butter beans left over. I served with pico de Gallo over the burgers and cooked corn.

Very good, although I changed a couple of things. I used panko bread crumbs instead of crackers. I omitted the cheese because I didn't have any. I added a fourth of a teaspoon onion powder. I let the mixture sit in the fridge for a few hours before forming the burgers (which helped a lot). And finally, I dipped the burgers in corn meal before frying. I served them on lightly toasted sesame seed buns with mayo, tomato slices and lettuce. They were delicious. Even the pickiest eater in the house liked 'em!

These were really yummy tasting, but they didnt stay together very well while cooking and were extremely oily. I used olive oil instead of vegetable oil...but other than that followed the recipe exactly. Next time I will probably follow suggestions to use either extra saltines, or bread crumbs, and bake them instead of frying.

So in all honesty, I'd give the taste a 5 and the texture a 2. I doubled the recipe and tried frying 1/2 and baking 1/2... neither batch stayed together :( but the taste is awesome! I use fresh garlic and added fresh parsley. Yum! Since I can't get it to stay together as a burger I think I'll double and bake as a veggie meatloaf from now on. You really can use any bean, cheese, or binder and it will taste good.

FAB! Now here's my verison:

1 (15 once) can butter beans
1/2 can Rainsed Black Beans
1/3 bread crumbs ur flavor choice
1/3 green peppers chopped
1/3 cup onion (white)
1/3 cup diced small celery
1/4 cup diced papaya 
1/3 cup diced carrot (I purchased the shredded carrots and ran a knife across them)
garlic powder/onion powder/ black pepper 

Mash beans with masher, add all the ingrediants one at a time while stiring them. Top with Mango chutney or eat plain. FAB!!!

I did do many changes but these are fabulous. I think since I made changes and still loved it it deserves 5 stars. My changes where I used white beans, I couldn't find butter and then once home it dawned on me I should have looked in the organic/health food area of the grocery. I also didn't want to buy more cheese so I used Colby Jack that I had and I don't like jalapeno so I used canned green chilies. I doubled the garlic powder too. Then I baked in the oven rather than pan fry. I loved these and can't wait to make them again and I will find the butter beans but keep to all the changes I made. Well maybe I will buy cheddar next time.
Loved it!! I did use harissa instead of jalapeño and oats instead of crackers, but this was definitely a big success!! Thank you for the inspiration!! 🫶

Made just as the recipe states. I might add a little worchestershire sauce next time, but these are awesome! I don't always have butter beans on hand. But I have Mayacoba and lima beans (dried) on hand that I may also have to substitute. Any experiences with substitutions? I live far from a store, so I often have to make do with substitutions. And I also made smaller, flatter patties to avoid it being mushy in the center. Delicious!!!
love these!
We really liked this recipe. Nice for a meatless meal. No changes, burgers are delicits as recipe is written!

Holey smokes!!! Thanks for the great idea and starting recipe. Not sure what a butter bean is but my favorite bean is the garbanzo so I substituted. No saltines so I substituted for 1/3 cup of breadcrumbs. No jalapeño darn it. I will use it next if I try to pick it up. All the rest is the same. Used a really hot skillet, sprayed it with Pam and cooked my burger. It was fantastic. This will definitely be in my weekly rotation. My husband hates garbanzo beans but when I tricked him with a bite he said he liked it until he found out what it was. Try it and add your own ingredients. I used lots of garlic and crushed red pepper. Yum!!!?
Added a LOT more crackers, bread crumbs, green chilis and Olives. Good base recipe to add to your liking....add grated veg or grain too! (april 2020)

One of our favorites! My son is vegetarian and I'm always on the lookout for something different. We always ate black bean burgers as our go to bean burger, but not anymore. We love these burgers. I use more jalapeno, two whole peppers, and my son has used pickled jalapenos in a pinch. I don't even eat them on a roll they are so good.

I am not a butter bean fan but he is. I was making these for the meat eating man and the veggie me. Not too often we can eat the same exact meal so this was nice. I added extra peppers, garlic and used panko and a mix of the cheeses I had in the fridge and they turned out nicely. Totally will make again!

I did not care for them. The first bite I thought was ok. The second bite made me nauseous and I couldn't eat anymore. I had been saving this recipe for a long time and was so excited to finally make them but I won't make them again.
